items.issue: The abstract does not explain why score ranking and held-out accuracy can differ.
items.selected_resolution: Name the two evaluation objects and state that a model can improve average quantile loss without uniformly improving calibration or every mechanism-specific score.
items.acceptance: The abstract is self-contained and contains no internal revision language.
validation: The abstract names computing time and held-out quantile loss as distinct evaluation objects; it is self-contained, 347 words, compiled, and visually inspected.

items.issue: Crossing and PriceFM results need a contribution-centered but evidence-bounded interpretation.
items.selected_resolution: Report the exact crossing tradeoff and the 6.687 versus 7.039 AQL comparison; describe the fixed-feature computational contrast without an unmeasured runtime claim.
items.acceptance: Claims match source numbers and do not call PriceFM categorically expensive.
validation: Crossing rates, six-of-eight oracle-score result, and 6.687 versus 7.039 AQL comparison match fixed Q--DESN commit aa613b0; no PriceFM runtime claim remains.

items.issue: Project-level attribution disclaimer weakens the contribution account.
items.selected_resolution: Remove the disclaimer and state documented antecedents and candidate contributions directly.
items.acceptance: No unsupported individual attribution is introduced.
validation: The project-level disclaimer is removed; antecedents and the candidate-confirmed exdqlm contribution are stated without unsupported ownership claims.

items.issue: The exdqlm contribution is incomplete and uses generic coauthor references.
items.selected_resolution: Name cited antecedents and document Antonio's restructuring, later LDVB and nonconjugate updates, compiled backends, filtering/smoothing corrections, forecasting, diagnostics, synthesis, and static RHS regression.
items.acceptance: The text does not claim the whole package is C++ or invent a speedup.
validation: Article, package NEWS, package source, focused tests, cited antecedents, and the candidate's clarification support the bounded contribution statement; whole-package C++ and measured-speedup claims are absent.

items.issue: Chapter 1 does not foreground the common non-mean inferential theme.
items.selected_resolution: Organize the opening around conditional quantiles, fixed-content intervals, and scalable computation for operational analysis.
items.acceptance: The common question precedes the project list and uses standard statistical terminology.
validation: The common question and non-mean distributional targets precede the project list; conditional quantiles and fixed-content intervals are distinguished explicitly.

items.issue: Acronyms are not always redefined at chapter first use.
items.selected_resolution: Audit and define field-specific acronyms independently in each reading unit.
items.acceptance: GloFAS, PriceFM, AL, exAL, ISVB, LDVB, MCMC, VB, DESN, RHS, MTI, AQL, CRPS, and PPLC are expanded or immediately explained at first use where present.
validation: Independent first-use audit completed for GloFAS, PriceFM, AL, exAL, ISVB, LDVB, MCMC, VB, DESN, RHS, MTI, AQL, CRPS, PPLC, ELBO, NWS, and USGS in every reading unit where used.

items.issue: The second objective omits scalable static regularized quantile regression and its role in DESN readouts.
items.selected_resolution: Add static AL/exAL regularized regression and connect it to high-dimensional reservoir readout fitting.
items.acceptance: The objective separates statistical target, software capability, and DESN use.
validation: Objective 2 now states scalable static regularized AL/exAL regression and its use for high-dimensional recurrent-feature readouts.

items.issue: Validation language alternates between vague robustness and overly defensive universal caveats.
items.selected_resolution: State empirical evidence under named designs and reserve consistency or general coverage for theorems; place material limitations once with the benefit and next step.
items.acceptance: No universal guarantee is implied and no result is followed by a redundant defensive disclaimer.
validation: Benefits, empirical units, inferential scope, and next checks are stated together; global searches found no vague robustness or unsupported consistency claim.

items.issue: Hydrology scope language does not connect the five-origin design to repeated dynamic-model computation.
items.selected_resolution: Explain the finite retrospective design and identify a matched MCMC comparison as future uncertainty-assessment work without claiming VB changes only uncertainty.
items.acceptance: The text distinguishes forecast accuracy, predictive calibration, and approximation uncertainty.
validation: Five origins are tied to repeated full dynamic-fit cost; forecast accuracy, calibration, and a future matched MCMC approximation study are distinguished.

items.issue: Chapter 3 uses informal author references and underdescribes ISVB and LDVB.
items.selected_resolution: Use citations to Yan, Zheng and Kottas and Barata, Prado and Sanso; define the approximations and distinguish inherited methods from later implementation work.
items.acceptance: No 'and coauthors' wording remains in the contribution account.
validation: Yan--Zheng--Kottas and Barata--Prado--Sansó are named with citations; ISVB and LDVB are expanded and inherited methods are separated from later software work.

items.issue: Section 1.3 is not sufficiently clear and its interval table is unnecessary.
items.selected_resolution: Replace Table 1.1 with prose that defines the target and interval distinctions and guides the later chapters.
items.acceptance: Label tab:intro-interval-objects is removed and no dangling reference remains.
validation: Table label tab:intro-interval-objects is absent; compact prose distinguishes credible, predictive, confidence, and tolerance intervals with no dangling reference.

items.issue: Future hydrologic covariates are described as summaries or ensembles rather than a deterministic path.
items.selected_resolution: State that one supplied deterministic precipitation and soil-water forecast path enters at each origin and its uncertainty is not propagated.
items.acceptance: No aggregation rule is guessed and post-origin gauge observations remain verification only.
validation: All current summaries state one deterministic precipitation and soil-water forecast path per origin, no propagated path uncertainty, and no guessed aggregation rule.

items.issue: Some model equation blocks are insufficiently interpreted.
items.selected_resolution: Add concise role statements before or after central equation blocks without duplicating derivations.
items.acceptance: Every central display is introduced by purpose and interpreted where its components are not self-evident.
validation: Central hydrology blocks now have explicit statistical roles; the other research chapters were audited for purpose-before-display and interpretation-after-display structure.

items.issue: Calligraphic notation may be visually overused.
items.selected_resolution: Retain standard probability and statistical notation; simplify only decorative index-set notation after a symbol-by-symbol audit.
items.acceptance: No global replacement changes mathematical meaning.
validation: Symbol-by-symbol review retained standard calligraphic probability and statistical objects; no global substitution or mathematical-object change was made.

items.issue: The hydrology seasonal periods lack their spectral-selection explanation.
items.selected_resolution: State that exploratory spectral peaks supplied the periods; interpret annual and semiannual components and leave the slow component phenomenological.
items.acceptance: Periods remain 363.59, 181.79, and 2474.87 days and no unsupported physical mechanism is added.
validation: The unchanged periods 363.59, 181.79, and 2474.87 days are tied to exploratory spectral peaks; physical interpretation is restricted to annual and semiannual components.

items.issue: Hydrology coverage fractions omit percentages and table bolding does not express the declared optimum.
items.selected_resolution: Add exact percentages and bold closest-to-95 coverage plus minimum interval score; do not bold width.
items.acceptance: All counts and scores are unchanged and the current projection hash is updated.
validation: Coverage cells contain 123/140 (87.9%), 132/140 (94.3%), 29/40 (72.5%), and 35/40 (87.5%); bolding follows closeness-to-95% and minimum-score criteria and the projection hash validates.

items.issue: Formatting and the treatment of bold run-in headings vary across chapters.
items.selected_resolution: Retain parallel contribution headings, review the exdqlm capability heading, and remove or promote MTI run-ins according to hierarchy.
items.acceptance: Heading levels reflect argument structure rather than visual emphasis.
validation: Four parallel contribution headings remain in the introduction, the exdqlm capability run-in was integrated, and four MTI run-ins were converted to continuous exposition.

items.issue: Tables 6.1 and D.1 need a clearer contribution and scientific-question structure.
items.selected_resolution: Redesign Table 6.1 around target, contribution, evidence, and scope; revise Table D.1 wording while preserving its label and four-column form.
items.acceptance: Both tables are compact, readable, and source-supported.
validation: Table 6.1 uses target, contribution, evidence, and scope columns; Table D.1 uses Scientific question and a positive caption; both compile without overflow and were visually inspected.

items.issue: The MTI data limitation is categorical and reads as a legal or regulatory disclaimer.
items.selected_resolution: Describe the overlapping partitions, dependence, ties, and measurement-definition limits, then identify prospective validation as the required extension.
items.acceptance: The contribution remains clear and no regulatory claim is implied.
validation: The pharmaceutical discussion states the exact data limits and specifies independent future batches, pre-recorded measurement definitions, and fixed grouping rules for prospective evaluation.

items.issue: The dissertation conclusion ends with a generic slogan.
items.selected_resolution: Conclude with the four projects' complementary contribution to target-specific distributional inference, computation, and validation.
items.acceptance: The final paragraph states substantive findings and future directions without hype.
validation: The conclusion synthesizes the four target-specific contributions and open validation questions; the generic computational-similarity slogan is absent.

items.issue: The full dissertation requires a consistency and anti-generic-prose pass.
items.selected_resolution: Remove internal workflow residue, generic transitions, repeated caveats, and unexplained technical shorthand by replacing them with object-level statistical prose.
items.acceptance: No concealment claim is made; prose is specific, restrained, and professionally self-contained.
validation: Chapter-by-chapter searches and final reading removed internal workflow residue, generic promotional language, unexplained shorthand, repeated defensive caveats, and unsupported engineering or machine-learning terminology; the factual assistance disclosure remains.

items.issue: The implementation needs a reproducible closeout and full manuscript validation.
items.selected_resolution: Update only current records affected by this pass, close all response items, validate source projections, build a release PDF, and inspect affected pages.
items.acceptance: All 22 items are IMPLEMENTED_VALIDATED, Bruno's 116 records remain intact, and release validation passes.
validation: All 22 items are closed; Bruno's 116-item immutable controls validate; 35 display records remain 33 KEEP and 2 OMIT; source projections, active TeX graph, release build, logs, fonts, page size, and affected rendered pages pass the recorded closeout checks.
